principle: Research results and market signals become product hypotheses, not automatic feature decisions.

current_direction.name: Studios, not dashboards
current_direction.summary: Wooolfmesh is exploring a simpler work environment where one focused Studio keeps the current task, selected memory, sources, AI, and durable output together. Secondary controls stay quiet until needed.
avoid: Separate AI destinations for every capability
A different bright color for every feature
New pages created only because a new backend object exists

evidence_levels.established: Supported by a review, meta-analysis, or repeated research.
evidence_levels.strong_signal: Useful experimental or field evidence, but context still matters.
evidence_levels.emerging: Recent evidence that needs more replication.

product_signals_2026.signal: Project-scoped context is becoming a primary product primitive
product_signals_2026.product_hypothesis: Every Studio should have a compact context packet so the user does not rebuild background information each time.

product_signals_2026.signal: Conversation and persistent work surface are separating
product_signals_2026.product_hypothesis: The artifact should be the main work surface. AI conversation should support it and be collapsible.

product_signals_2026.signal: Agent work is becoming recurring, inspectable, and attached to workspace context
product_signals_2026.product_hypothesis: Recurring agent work should appear as Runs inside the Studio it serves, not in a separate automation control room.

product_signals_2026.signal: Information-dense products are deliberately calming their chrome
product_signals_2026.product_hypothesis: Navigation, separators, and icons should recede after the user reaches the work surface.

product_signals_2026.signal: Expressive design is being used to direct attention, not color every object
product_signals_2026.product_hypothesis: Use a calm neutral base and reserve stronger color, size, shape, and motion for the primary action or meaningful state.

product_signals_2026.signal: Voice is returning as a lightweight work input
product_signals_2026.product_hypothesis: Voice can later become a thin capture and steering layer over Studios instead of a separate product mode.

facts_2026.fact: Participants in a CHI 2026 field study switched browser tabs more than 60 times per hour during knowledge work.
facts_2026.implication: A Studio should bring active task context, sources, notes, memory, and output together to reduce context switching.

facts_2026.fact: In a field experiment across 66 firms and 7,137 knowledge workers, treated users who adopted integrated generative AI spent about two fewer hours on email per week, while task composition did not materially change.
facts_2026.implication: Target overhead around existing work before inventing more work categories and dashboards.

facts_2026.fact: Google reports that participants found key interface elements up to four times faster in some Material 3 Expressive eye-tracking tests.
facts_2026.implication: Strong visual hierarchy can make the primary action easier to find without adding more controls.

facts_2026.fact: A preregistered 2026 study found a speedup illusion: participants expected AI-assisted simple tasks to be faster even when measured completion times were similar; subjective effort was lower with AI.
facts_2026.implication: Measure completed outcomes and reduced friction rather than AI activity, token volume, or perceived speed alone.

studio_hypotheses.name: One Studio shell
studio_hypotheses.idea: Use one consistent work shell instead of many feature pages. The center is current work; AI, memory, sources, task state, and history are contextual layers.
studio_hypotheses.test: Can a user complete a real task without navigating away from the Studio?

studio_hypotheses.name: Minimum viable context packet
studio_hypotheses.idea: Keep only goal, current state, next action, decisions, useful sources, and selected memory close to the work.
studio_hypotheses.test: Generate the packet automatically and let the user correct it.

studio_hypotheses.name: Artifact-first work
studio_hypotheses.idea: Keep the durable output persistent while AI works around it. Do not force the result back into a chat transcript.
studio_hypotheses.test: Use a dominant work surface with an optional AI panel that can collapse completely.

studio_hypotheses.name: Resume line
studio_hypotheses.idea: Keep one short exact next physical action for every active Studio.
studio_hypotheses.test: Show it when reopening a Studio and after interruptions.

studio_hypotheses.name: Quiet memory
studio_hypotheses.idea: Retrieve one to three high-signal memories only when they can change the current decision.
studio_hypotheses.test: Keep memory hidden by default and show a short relevance reason when it appears.

studio_hypotheses.name: Risk-based agent checkpoints
studio_hypotheses.idea: Confirmation frequency should depend on action risk, reversibility, uncertainty, and user preference.
studio_hypotheses.test: Compare end-only approval, every-step approval, and risk-based checkpoints.

visual_hypothesis.name: Calm base, expressive action
visual_hypothesis.note: This is a design hypothesis, not a neuroscience claim.
rules: Keep most of the interface neutral.
Use one strong accent for the current primary action or selected state.
Use semantic colors for meaning, not decoration.
Do not rely on color alone to communicate status.

studies.finding: People often move information into external tools to reduce the amount they must keep active in their mind.
studies.product_hypothesis: Capture should be extremely fast. Structure can come later. Wooolfmesh should remember commitments, context, and next steps so the user does not have to keep rehearsing them mentally.
studies.test: Test a one-action capture inbox with later clarification and a visible confirmation that the item is safely stored.
studies.citation: Risko, E. F., & Gilbert, S. J. (2016). Cognitive Offloading.

studies.finding: When people leave unfinished work, part of their attention can stay with the previous task and reduce performance on the next task.
studies.product_hypothesis: A Studio should protect the active task while making interruptions safe to capture without opening another work stream.
studies.test: Keep interruption capture inside the Studio and close work with outcome, next action, and an exact resume point.
studies.citation: Leroy, S. (2009). Why is it so hard to do my work? The challenge of attention residue when switching between work tasks.

studies.finding: If-then plans can help people translate goals into action by connecting a situation with a planned response.
studies.product_hypothesis: Background Runs can be linked to clear local triggers instead of requiring a separate routines dashboard.
studies.test: Test local trigger rules inside the relevant Studio. Durable changes stay preview-first.
studies.citation: Gollwitzer, P. M., & Sheeran, P. (2006). Implementation Intentions and Goal Achievement: A Meta-analysis of Effects and Processes.

studies.finding: Trying to recall information can improve later retention more than simply reading the same material again.
studies.product_hypothesis: Memory should sometimes help the user retrieve a lesson, not only display it.
studies.test: Test an optional Recall first interaction for important lessons linked to the current Studio.
studies.citation: Roediger, H. L., & Karpicke, J. D. (2006). Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention.

studies.finding: A CHI 2025 study found that higher confidence in generative AI was linked with less reported critical-thinking effort. Critical thinking also moved toward verification, integration, and supervision.
studies.product_hypothesis: AI should make verification easy and keep the user responsible for important decisions instead of only producing polished answers.
studies.test: Show sources, assumptions, and verify-before-apply cues for higher-impact AI suggestions.
studies.citation: Lee et al. (2025). The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking.

studies.topic: Autonomous versus dependent cognitive offloading to AI
studies.finding: A 2026 study distinguishes AI that substitutes for the user's core thinking from AI that scaffolds thinking while the user retains cognitive agency.
studies.product_hypothesis: AI should sometimes structure, challenge, retrieve, or verify rather than immediately produce the final answer.
studies.test: Offer help-me-think and first-pass behaviors inside the same Studio rather than creating more AI pages.
studies.citation: Zhu et al. (2026). Not all cognitive offloading is equal: distinguishing dependent and autonomous offloading to generative AI.

studies.finding: Research on daily-assistant agents found that plan quality and user involvement both matter. Plausible-looking plans can still create misplaced trust.
studies.product_hypothesis: Agent work should be inspectable before execution and easy to steer while it runs.
studies.test: Use Plan -> Preview -> Run -> Checkpoint -> Result and keep a local action log.

studies.finding: A 2026 productivity-agent study found lower workload with agentic support while user preference for control influenced trust. Other 2026 work shows that oversight itself can create workload.
studies.product_hypothesis: Useful control is not manual versus fully autonomous. Confirmation should adapt to the action.
studies.test: Use checkpoints based on risk, reversibility, uncertainty, and user preference.
studies.citation: Geninatti Cossatin et al. (2026). The autonomy equation.

research_backlog: Runs attached to their Studio instead of an automation dashboard
Voice capture and steering as a later thin input layer
Calm neutral palette with one expressive action color
